methodological_questions: How to define similarity of pre-absence initiation profiles

historical_evidence.finding: Tested whether having a similar-profile teammate separates absorption from cascade when a player sits. Mean similarity ABSORBED +0.863 vs CASCADE +0.848; Spearman(sim, -gap) = -0.19 (wrong-signed). Embiid 23-24 cascades with Reed sim 0.94. Adequately powered null result; similarity does not separate outcomes and is almost always findable.

Connector absence displaces team offensive identity more than usage-matched non-organizer absence (paired dD_A +0.1151, t=6.35, p=7.35e-09, n=96 matched pairs). Demonstrates measurable reorganization with a larger sample, but identity displacement is role-specific.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Using overall initiation-profile similarity to classify absence outcomes as absorption or cascade
failed_approaches.why: Similarity does not separate absorption from cascade (adequately powered null); limited by LABEL_ERROR.

evidence_establishes: Overall initiation-profile similarity of a teammate does not predict whether the team absorbs or cascades the absent player's play types (FAM:SF-CHT-052).
Large-scale reorganization after a player absence is detectable only with substantial sample sizes (n~96 in SF-APPS-088) and for specific player roles.
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether the most similar teammate specifically gains share in the absent player's primary play types.
Whether alternative similarity definitions (minutes, initiations, same-position minutes) improve prediction.
Whether the gain magnitude correlates with similarity across spells.
Whether the available 11 cases can support any reliable inference.
own_inferences: The 11 cases likely represent a highly filtered subset (e.g., multi-game absences of primary initiators with a clear most-similar replacement), which would severely limit generalizability and power.
Noise in initiation-profile estimates from limited pre-absence games may dominate any signal, especially with only 11 spells.
The question is conceptually testable with a much larger dataset (e.g., 100+ absence spells of high-usage players with well-defined primary types), but not with the current data as described.
uncertainties: The exact composition of the 11 cases (which players, how many games per spell).
Whether primary types are defined as top-1, top-3, or a percentage threshold, and whether they are stable.
Whether 'gain' is measured as absolute count, per-possession rate, or proportion of team initiations.
How similarity is operationalized (cosine distance, Euclidean, Jensen-Shannon) and whether it is computed on proportions or raw counts.
Whether the dataset contains enough games to estimate profiles reliably for each player.

historical_effect.explanation: Even without the prior null, the sample size of 11 cases alone would be insufficient. The historical evidence reinforces that overall similarity does not predict absorption/cascade and that meaningful reorganization effects require much larger samples.

blocking_constraints.text: Only 11 cases are recorded as available; any prospective test would be severely underpowered to detect a plausible effect size.
Initiation profiles estimated from limited pre-absence games may be too noisy to produce reliable similarity rankings.
Opponent quality, game script, other injuries, and schematic adjustments confound the estimated gain in primary types.
Rare play types may have close-to-zero baseline volume for the replacement teammate, making proportional gains unreliable.
Defining 'primary types' and 'most similar teammate' involves arbitrary thresholds that can misclassify cases.

prior_work.summary: FAM:SF-CHT-052 directly addressed whether overall similarity predicts absorption vs cascade and found no effect. The current question refines this to gains in primary types for the most similar teammate, but no study has directly tested that. FAM:SF-APPS-088 shows that connector absence causes identity displacement, implying organizational change is measurable only with adequate sample size and role-specific hypotheses.

risks.text: Only 11 cases available, far below the ~96 matched pairs needed for a detectable displacement effect in prior work.
Low reliability of initiation-profile similarity when based on fewer than 20 games; pre-absence windows may be short.
Opponent strength, home/road, back-to-back, and concurrent injuries will confound gain estimates if not controlled.
If the absent player's primary type is infrequent for the replacement teammate, gain may be bounded by zero-floor.
Arbitrary choice of primary-type threshold (e.g., top-2 vs top-3) changes the set of outcomes and which teammate is tagged as closest.
Testing multiple play types and multiple teammate candidates per spell inflates false positive risk.

design.estimand: For each absence spell, the difference in volume (per 100 team possessions) of the absent player's primary play types between (a) the most-similar teammate and (b) the average volume of other active teammates, measured during the absence window, expressed as a standardized effect size across spells.
design.unit: A player absence spell (contiguous games missed by one player due to injury, rest, or suspension) with at least 4 games missed and at least 10 games of pre-absence data for the absent player and each candidate teammate.
design.sample: All spells from the 2022-23 through 2025-26 seasons meeting criteria, yielding a minimum of 40 spells after exclusions. The current 11 cases would not suffice; expansion is needed.
design.power: A minimum of 40 spells provides 80% power to detect a correlation of r=0.40 between similarity rank and gain rank at alpha=0.05 (one-sided), based on Fisher's transformation.
design.controls: Opponent defensive rating, venue, rest advantage, and number of other absent rotation players included as covariates in a mixed-effects model.
design.falsification: Test whether the least-similar teammate shows a smaller gain than the most-similar; and whether gains in non-primary play types do not differ systematically.
design.multiplicity: Primary outcome is a single rank correlation across spells; secondary play-type-specific tests corrected via Holm-Bonferroni.
design.decision_rule: Proceed only if the effective sample size after exclusions reaches 40 spells and pre-registration thresholds are met; otherwise do not proceed.
design.data_version: NBA 2022-23 through 2025-26 per-game play-by-play and derived play-type initiation records as of 2026-11-01.
